Igneo Infrastructure Partners has raised €6bn for its fourth European infrastructure fund, beating its €4bn target by 50% and reaching its hard cap just six months after first close.

Swiss alternative investment manager LGT Capital Partners has appointed long-serving executive Sascha Gruber as its next chief executive, succeeding Roberto Paganoni after almost three decades leading the $120bn-plus investment business.

New York-based pharmaceutical developer Formation Bio has secured $600m in commitments for its first dedicated drug development investment fund, targeting the acquisition of up to 15 clinical-stage medicines over the next five years.

Thrive Holdings has agreed to acquire US home security provider ADT in a $15.3bn take-private transaction, comprising approximately $7.6bn of equity value and $7.7bn of net debt.

Clayton, Dubilier & Rice has reportedly gathered about $20bn for its thirteenth flagship buyout fund in just six months, twice the amount raised over a comparable period for its $26bn predecessor in 2023.

Dubai-based venture capital firm BY Venture Partners has closed its third fund at $60m, 20% larger than its predecessor, as it expands its European investment operations with a new office in Lisbon.

Lightspeed Venture Partners has reportedly raised more than $750m for a new fund and co-investment vehicle targeting acquisitions of established businesses which can be transformed through AI, as the venture capital heavyweight expands further into private equity-style buyouts.

US commercial real estate lender ACORE Capital has raised $1.1bn for its second opportunistic credit fund, more than quadrupling the size of its predecessor as it targets financing opportunities created by property market dislocation.

San Francisco-based U&I Ventures has closed its oversubscribed debut fund on $32.2m, with plans to back up to 45 early-stage AI infrastructure startups through an investment strategy informed by a network of 1,800 senior enterprise technology executives.

Dutch private equity firm HC Partners has almost doubled the size of its flagship fund after raising €100m for its third vehicle, exceeding its original €80m target and securing commitments from all of its existing institutional investors.
